accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the outcome in Junagadh in 1947–48?
o: The Nawab acceded to Pakistan and continued to rule after the plebiscite
The Nawab acceded to India and a plebiscite confirmed accession to Pakistan
The Nawab acceded to Pakistan, fled after an economic blockade, and a plebiscite was held in February 1948
The Nawab remained independent and joined the Rajasthan Union in 1949
accepted.x: Junagadh’s Nawab acceded to Pakistan in September 1947. Following an economic blockade and his flight, a plebiscite was held in February 1948 in favour of India.
accepted.tq: Test the sequence of ruler, decision, crisis and final settlement rather than recalling a single date.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who was the Dewan of Junagadh at the time of its accession to Pakistan?
accepted.x: Shah Nawaz Bhutto was the Dewan of Junagadh under Nawab Mahabat Khanji III.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–Dewan association to avoid the common wrong-person trap.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: The accession of Junagadh to Pakistan took place in:
accepted.x: Junagadh acceded to Pakistan in September 1947; the plebiscite favouring India was held later, in February 1948.
accepted.tq: Separate the accession date from the later plebiscite date.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bhopal — merged with India in October 1949
Manipur and Tripura — merged with India in 1949 through merger agreements
Hyderabad — merged through a plebiscite in February 1948
Kashmir — joined India without conditions under its Dewan
accepted.x: Manipur and Tripura entered into merger agreements and merged with India in October 1949. The other pairs incorrectly interchange the methods or dates of integration.
accepted.tq: Match each state with its distinctive method and timing of integration.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the integration of princely states:
1. Bhopal was merged with India in 1949.
2. Manipur and Tripura were merged in October 1949.
3. Travancore joined India without conditions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Bhopal merged in 1949, Manipur and Tripura merged in October 1949 through merger agreements, and Travancore joined India without conditions.
accepted.tq: Check each state against its separate method or date before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: The approximate number of princely states involved in the integration process, as generally used in this context, was:
accepted.x: The figure generally used here is about 562 princely states. Other figures occur in different accounts, but 562 is the prescribed figure in this context.
accepted.tq: Identify the prescribed approximate figure while distinguishing it from nearby alternative counts.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: By 15 August 1947, which one of the following groups is identified as having remained outside accession to India?
accepted.x: The standard account identifies Kashmir, Hyderabad and Junagadh as the states that had not signed accession by 15 August 1947. Some Andhra history accounts additionally mention Travancore as a fourth hold-out.
accepted.tq: Watch for the distinction between the standard three-state account and the additional regional listing.
accepted.sec: ■ States → method and timing of integration  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the principal method used in the integration of princely states?
o: Direct administration by the United Nations
Persuasion, patriotic appeals and, where necessary, pressure or force
Abolition of all rulers before accession
accepted.x: The States Department used persuasion and patriotic appeals, along with the threat of popular uprisings or force where necessary. Privy purses and internal autonomy were also offered.
accepted.tq: Apply the broad policy description rather than choosing an extreme ‘only’ method.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the office-holders of the States Department?
o: V.P. Menon as head and Sardar Patel as Secretary
Jawaharlal Nehru as head and C.P. Ramaswami Iyer as negotiator
Sardar Patel as head and V.P. Menon as Secretary and chief negotiator
Rajendra Prasad as head and Hamidullah Khan as Secretary
accepted.x: Sardar Patel, the Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister, headed the States Department. V.P. Menon served as its Secretary and chief negotiator.
accepted.tq: Use the authority–subordinate role distinction to defeat a swapped-office option.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, a princely state could:
o: Transfer its decision to the United Nations
Join India, join Pakistan or remain independent
accepted.x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, allowed princely states to join India, join Pakistan or remain independent.
accepted.tq: Test the complete three-way choice instead of confusing legal options with the later political outcome.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the subjects ceded to the Centre through the Instrument of Accession?
accepted.x: The Instrument of Accession initially transferred Defence, External Affairs and Communications to the Centre. Internal autonomy was retained by the rulers at that stage.
accepted.tq: Find the exception by separating the three ceded subjects from the retained internal autonomy.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: The concessions offered to the rulers in connection with accession included:
o: Membership of the Union Cabinet and judicial immunity
Permanent independence from the Indian Union
Control over Defence and External Affairs
accepted.x: The rulers were offered privy purses and internal autonomy in return for accession, while Defence, External Affairs and Communications were ceded to the Centre.
accepted.tq: Match the political incentive with the powers actually transferred to the Centre.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Travancore and Jodhpur issues is correct?
o: The Dewan of Travancore declared independence, while Jinnah attempted to attract the Maharaja of Jodhpur
The Maharaja of Travancore negotiated with the United Nations, while Patel attracted Jodhpur to Pakistan
Travancore joined Pakistan and Jodhpur remained independent
Both states were merged into Hyderabad before accession
accepted.x: Dewan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer declared Travancore’s independence, partly in the context of its thorium wealth. Maharaja Hanwant Singh of Jodhpur was tempted by Jinnah.
accepted.tq: Keep separate the two problem states and identify the correct person–state association.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following phases of integration described by V.P. Menon in the chronological order:
A. Democratisation
B. Abolition of privy purses
C. Extinction of small states through merger into provinces
D. Consolidation into unions
accepted.x: Menon’s four phases were extinction, consolidation into unions, democratisation and finally abolition of privy purses.
accepted.tq: Fix the first phase as extinction and the final phase as abolition, then arrange the middle stages.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT cited as an example of consolidation into unions during the integration process?
accepted.x: The examples given for consolidation into unions were Saurashtra, Rajasthan Union, PEPSU and Madhya Bharat. Hyderabad Union was not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Use the named-list exception method and identify the option absent from the recognised union examples.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: The office of Rajpramukh was associated with:
accepted.x: Rajpramukhs were the heads of Part B states, which consisted of former princely states or unions. The office ended under the Seventh Amendment in 1956.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional category with its distinctive head rather than with the former provincial categories.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: The office of Rajpramukh was abolished or ended through the:
accepted.x: The office of Rajpramukh ended through the Seventh Amendment of 1956. The Twenty-sixth Amendment of 1971 dealt with privy purses and royal titles.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the amendment connected with Rajpramukhs from the later amendment abolishing privy purses.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: Privy purses and the official recognition of royal titles were abolished by the:
accepted.x: The Twenty-sixth Amendment Act, 1971, abolished privy purses and royal titles. It was enacted during Indira Gandhi’s tenure.
accepted.tq: Separate the amendment number and year from other constitutional amendments of the same period.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which Articles were omitted in connection with the abolition of privy purses?
accepted.x: The Twenty-sixth Amendment omitted Articles 291 and 362, which were associated with privy purses and the privileges of former rulers.
accepted.tq: Use the exact Article-number pair rather than relying only on the amendment number.
accepted.sec: ■ Privy purses and Rajpramukhs  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Part A, Part B, Part C and Part D classification in 1950?
o: Part A—former Governor’s provinces; Part B—former princely states or unions with Rajpramukhs; Part C—former Chief Commissioners’ provinces and some princely states; Part D—Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Part A—Chief Commissioners’ provinces; Part B—Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part C—Governor’s provinces; Part D—princely unions
Part A—former princely states; Part B—former Governor’s provinces; Part C—foreign territories; Part D—Hyderabad
Part A—princely unions; Part B—Governor’s provinces; Part C—Andaman and Nicobar Islands; Part D—Chief Commissioners’ provinces
accepted.x: Part A comprised former Governor’s provinces; Part B comprised former princely states or unions headed by Rajpramukhs; Part C included former Chief Commissioners’ provinces and some princely states; Part D consisted of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
accepted.tq: Read the classification as a four-column comparison and eliminate options with shifted categories.
accepted.sec: ■ Instrument of Accession; Part A, B, C, D states

accepted.s: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession of Jammu and Kashmir after:
o: A Pakistani-backed tribal invasion in October 1947
The United Nations ceasefire of January 1949
accepted.x: Maharaja Hari Singh hesitated initially but signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947 after the Pakistani-backed tribal invasion. Indian troops were then airlifted to Srinagar.
accepted.tq: Connect the triggering event with the constitutional act instead of treating accession as an isolated date.
accepted.sec: ■ Jammu and Kashmir accession - ruler, invasion, date, UN  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sequence in the Jammu and Kashmir crisis?
o: UN ceasefire, tribal invasion, accession, airlift of troops
Tribal invasion, accession, airlift of troops, First Indo-Pak war
Accession, UN reference, tribal invasion, airlift of troops
Airlift of troops, accession, tribal invasion, UN ceasefire
accepted.x: The sequence was tribal invasion, Instrument of Accession, airlifting of Indian troops to Srinagar and the First Indo-Pak war. The UN ceasefire followed in January 1949.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence with the invasion first and the ceasefire last.
accepted.sec: ■ Jammu and Kashmir accession - ruler, invasion, date, UN  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who referred the Jammu and Kashmir issue to the United Nations?
accepted.x: Jawaharlal Nehru referred the Kashmir issue to the United Nations on 1 January 1948. Patel preferred a military solution.
accepted.tq: Use the decision-maker versus preferred-policy distinction to avoid a swapped-leader trap.
accepted.sec: ■ Jammu and Kashmir accession - ruler, invasion, date, UN  [other exams]

accepted.s: The United Nations ceasefire in the first Indo-Pak war over Jammu and Kashmir took place in:
accepted.x: The United Nations ceasefire took place in January 1949. The Instrument of Accession had been signed earlier, on 26 October 1947, and the issue was referred to the UN on 1 January 1948.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the accession, UN reference and ceasefire dates in the same episode.
accepted.sec: ■ Jammu and Kashmir accession - ruler, invasion, date, UN  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Kashmir issue is correct?
o: Patel referred the issue to the UN and Nehru preferred a military solution
Nehru referred the issue to the UN and Patel preferred a military solution
Hari Singh referred the issue to the UN and Menon commanded the Indian Army
The UN imposed a ceasefire before the Instrument of Accession was signed
accepted.x: Nehru referred the Kashmir issue to the UN, whereas Patel preferred a military solution. The Instrument of Accession preceded the January 1949 ceasefire.
accepted.tq: Test a paired contrast between two leaders and their positions.
accepted.sec: ■ Jammu and Kashmir accession - ruler, invasion, date, UN  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly identifies the authorship and authors of the two works associated with Hyderabad and state integration?
o: The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — V.P. Menon; Hyderabad in Retrospect — Laik Ali
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Sardar Patel; Hyderabad in Retrospect — Moin Nawaz Jung
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Laik Ali; Hyderabad in Retrospect — V.P. Menon
The Story of the Integration of the Indian States — Jawaharlal Nehru; Hyderabad in Retrospect — C.P. Ramaswami Iyer
accepted.x: V.P. Menon wrote The Story of the Integration of the Indian States. Hyderabad in Retrospect was written by Laik Ali, the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use author–work matching and guard against swapping the two titles.
accepted.sec: ■ States Department - Patel and V.P. Menon  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948?
accepted.x: Moin Nawaz Jung led the Nizam’s delegation to the United Nations Security Council in 1948.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Hyderabad diplomat from the Prime Minister, Dewan and Indian negotiator names.
accepted.sec: ■ Hyderabad's UN appeal and accounts  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Laik Ali, who wrote Hyderabad in Retrospect, was the:
accepted.x: Laik Ali was the last Prime Minister of Hyderabad and authored Hyderabad in Retrospect.
accepted.tq: Link the author with his precise office rather than with another integration-era official.
accepted.sec: ■ Hyderabad's UN appeal and accounts  [APPSC]
